A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPD-Min-ESTR study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G report original simulations, regret and runtime comparisons, empirical curvature estimates, and experiments on real-world graph topologies.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix G.6 adds experiments comparing online methods with an offline baseline.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes 'without replacement' from its exploratory sampling example, a limited sampling-instruction correction consistent with the existing i.i.d. analysis. Nuclear-norm estimation, eigenvector-based rotation, the 2|V|-1-dimensional representation, and the linear-bandit stage remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Erdős–Rényi and stochastic block models and the same four real-world networks. The new offline comparison reuses the homophilic stochastic-block-model task; it adds settings and results without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix G.6 newly evaluates the offline SDP-based method attributed to Chaitanya et al. (2024) against the proposed method and oracle subspace OFUL. Previously, that method was discussed but not experimentally compared. Existing OFUL and oracle comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New G.6 uses T=250, T1=50, noise σ=10^-4, 100 arms, and minimum objective achieved so far on 16- and 32-node graphs. Existing experiments retain their protocols. G.4 additionally specifies 2|V| edge updates per real-data arm, conflicting with the |V| specification retained in Table 1; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The empirical RSC diagnostic, scalability study, polarized-opinion analysis, and noise/arm-count sensitivity analyses in G.1–G.5 are retained. G.6 adds a baseline comparison rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: G.6 reports 500 trials for each new configuration. The existing 100-run experiments, 25-trial curvature estimates, and standard-deviation or confidence-interval reporting remain unchanged; there is no reported increase in repetitions for existing results.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds objective trajectories below the offline baseline and mean final objectives: OURS/ORACLE are 2.71/2.64 for 16 nodes and 3.09/3.05 for 32 nodes. These are new comparisons under a separate protocol. Figures 1–4 and Table 2 retain their earlier numerical results.

T1.justification: Remark 1 and Proposition 5 replace the minimum eigenvalue of the full vectorized-arm covariance with an infimum of normalized quadratic measurements over the error cone. Definition 4 restricts that cone to symmetric matrices, and Proposition 7 changes its RSC requirement from all matrices to the cone. These substantially revise the theoretical conditions and supporting argument, although the displayed regret-rate formula is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly state the bound O-tilde(max{1/κ, sqrt(|V|)} sqrt(|V|T)), exposing intervention-diversity dependence omitted from their earlier summaries. This refines the headline guarantee already given in Theorem 4.1; the central online formulation, dimensionality reduction, and empirical-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds reasons for choosing sequential regret minimization over best-arm identification or batching and interprets G.6 as evidence for the benefit of sequential feedback. Its new ethics statement discusses objective reversal for manipulation, privileged platform access, and user-autonomy risks. Existing empirical interpretations and future-work limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 replaces the anonymous code-access pointer with a named GitHub repository. V2 adds a reproducibility statement and an explicit real-data arm-construction description, although the latter conflicts with Table 1. Existing solver, environment, and hyperparameter documentation is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lee et al. (2026), gives the already-cited Chen et al. (2018) a clearer role in the incomplete-information literature, and revises the discussion of Jang et al. (2024). Section 1 and Appendix A now distinguish optimal-design approaches and discuss full-span requirements and O(|V|^6) computational cost.

P1.justification: V2 corrects grammar and terminology, frequently replaces 'users' with 'agents,' updates affiliations, and expands several explanatory passages. Reproducibility and ethics statements and G.6 are added, while the main section order and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into the ICLR format, changing typography, heading styles, running headers, text width, and figure/table sizing and placement throughout. Table 1 is integrated with the implementation text instead of occupying a separate page. A new two-panel Figure 5 is added; existing plots and tables retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision through the explicit diversity-dependent headline bound and better alignment of the RSC statements with the structured error cone. It also adds a relevant offline comparison and clearer research positioning. The gains are limited: existing benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the new real-data arm-generation description conflicts with Table 1, leaving a reproducibility ambiguity.
